name: AlertDialog
summary: A modal question about an action that cannot be undone. The person must answer it: Cancel or the action. It never closes on a click outside.
useWhen: An action deletes or overwrites something for good and there is no undo
An action affects other people at once: removing a member, revoking a link
Leaving a flow would throw away work that cannot be saved as a draft
avoidWhen: The action can be undone: run it and offer undo
The question needs fields or more than a short description
A message that needs no answer
Asking about a routine action the person runs many times a day

onOpenChange.description: Called with false for Escape, Cancel and the action.

size.description: The width from the dialog.width tokens: 360 and 440 px, never wider than the viewport minus a gutter.

tone.description: danger: the action destroys something. The title and the icon take the danger color; the action Button should be tone danger, emphasis solid.

dismissible.description: false: Escape does nothing. For the short wait while the action runs; the app sets it back to true when the action ends.

title.description: AlertDialogContent: the title for the common case, the same as an AlertDialogTitle child.

description.description: AlertDialogContent: the description for the common case.

icon.description: AlertDialogContent: a system icon name or a node above the title, hidden from assistive tech. false shows none.

rootProps.description: AlertDialogContent: props for the root layer. className and style go to the root too; ref and every other prop go to the panel, Radix Content props included (onOpenAutoFocus, onCloseAutoFocus, onEscapeKeyDown).

AlertDialogTrigger.description: One child element, a system Button, rendered as the trigger (always asChild). Focus returns to it on close.

AlertDialogCancel.description: One child element, a system Button: the safe answer. It closes the alert dialog and takes focus when it opens. Marked data-dialog-cancel.

AlertDialogAction.description: One child element, a system Button that names the consequence. It closes the alert dialog on click; call event.preventDefault() in onClick to keep it open while the action runs.

a11y.role: alertdialog (the panel), modal: Radix hides the rest of the page from assistive tech and keeps focus inside. Named by the title (aria-labelledby), described by the description (aria-describedby).
a11y.focus: On open, focus goes to an element marked data-autofocus, else to the Cancel action, in every tone, so Enter never runs the action by accident. On close, focus returns to the trigger, or to the element that had focus before; when that is gone, to its nearest connected focusable ancestor, else the first tab stop of main, else the body.

keys.Escape: Cancels and closes the alert dialog, unless dismissible is false
keys.Tab: Moves between Cancel and the action inside the alert dialog and wraps from the last to the first
keys.Shift+Tab: Moves back inside the alert dialog and wraps from the first to the last
keys.Enter: Runs the focused button: Cancel when the alert dialog opens

a11y.announce: The role alertdialog, the title and the description are read when it opens. An error after a failed action goes in the description with role alert.
notes: No close part and no close on a backdrop click: the question is answered with Cancel or the action. Escape is the same as Cancel.
The page behind does not scroll while it is open (Radix scroll lock).
Toasts sit above it and stay readable and clickable, as with Dialog.
The icon is decoration and hidden from assistive tech; the title carries the meaning.

Order 1.23 motion: a backdrop press never closes an alert dialog; the panel nudges once along the inline axis to say so (interaction dialog-refuse), and stays still under reduced motion. The backdrop blurs the page in and the parts read within 200ms.

Order 1.29, optional parts titlebar and controls (the Dialog pattern): rendered only when the active style lists them under optionalParts["alert-dialog"] in its style.json. The title bar holds the title (a direct AlertDialogTitle child or the title prop, still the accessible name); with controls it starts with WindowControls, whose close light cancels (as Escape and Cancel do), and minimize and zoom are idle and out of the tab order. No style turns them on yet.
Order 1.29, review 3 B8: a refused backdrop press keeps focus where it was (WCAG 2.4.3): its pointerdown and mousedown defaults are prevented, so focus never falls to the body.

en.title: The question, naming the action and its object, in sentence case: Delete the board Spring launch?
en.description: What is lost, and that it cannot be undone: Its 12 frames and every comment are deleted for good. An error after a failed action is added inside the description, in a role alert element that is there from the start.
en.buttons: The action names the consequence: Delete board, Remove member. Cancel keeps the object: Keep board. Never OK, Yes, Continue or Confirm.
en.error: Could not delete the team. Check your connection, then try again.

ar.title: The question in white Saudi dialect, no diacritics: تبي تحذف لوحة إطلاق الربيع؟
ar.description: بتنحذف 12 إطار وكل التعليقات، وما تقدر ترجعها بعدين.
ar.buttons: Noun form labels: حذف اللوحة، إبقاء اللوحة. Never نعم or موافق.
ar.error: ما قدرنا نحذف الفريق. تأكد من الاتصال وجرب مرة ثانية.

react.note: Built on DialogBase (Dialog folder): the themed portal, the focus rule and return, toasts above. Styled by the alert-dialog block of Dialog.css.

angular.note: On the Angular Dialog layer, role alertdialog, no close part, no backdrop close.

styles.studio: The dialog panel without a title band: a tinted disc with the icon, the title and the description on the surface, the footer band on surface-2 with Cancel and the action. Danger tints the disc and the title.
styles.desk: The Desk dialog glass, radius and window shadow, with no title bar: an alert is not a window. It grows from 92% on the window open timing.

mistakes.wrong: An alert dialog for an action that has undo
mistakes.right: Run the action and show a Toast with an Undo action

mistakes.wrong: Buttons that say Yes and No
Focus on the action when it opens
mistakes.right: AlertDialogCancel around the safe Button: focus opens on it

mistakes.wrong: A close button in the corner
mistakes.right: Cancel is the way out; there is no close part

mistakes.wrong: Closing the alert while the action is still running
mistakes.right: event.preventDefault() in the action's onClick, dismissible false and the Button loading until it ends
